title: ASSIGNMENT – 5
subtitle: Binary Classification using Naive Bayes and K-Nearest Neighbors
name: Srikrishna O S

sections.heading: AIM
sections.paragraph: To implement Naive Bayes and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) classifiers for a binary classification problem, evaluate them using multiple performance metrics, visualize model behavior, and analyze overfitting, underfitting, and bias-variance characteristics.

plots.caption: KNN accuracy vs number of neighbors

rows: Loaded 4601 samples with 57 features from Kaggle Spambase
Compared accuracy, precision, recall, F1 across variants
GridSearchCV and RandomizedSearchCV over k, weights, metric
Best k identified, cross-validation accuracy reported
Compared neighbor search algorithms for KNN
Measured training and prediction times for both
Plotted confusion matrices, ROC curves, accuracy vs k
All plots saved in results/ directory
Discussed overfitting for small k, underfitting for large k
Optimal k balances bias and variance

sections.heading: LEARNING OUTCOMES
bullets: Implemented Naive Bayes variants (Gaussian, Multinomial, Bernoulli) and compared their performance
Built KNN classifier and tuned hyperparameters using GridSearchCV and RandomizedSearchCV
Compared KDTree and BallTree neighbor search algorithms for computational efficiency
Analyzed bias-variance tradeoff by varying k and observing training vs validation accuracy
Generated and interpreted confusion matrices and ROC curves for model evaluation
